definition: A fixed-length value created from data that cannot be turned back into the original.
exampleSentence: Comparing the hash of two files is a quick way to see if they differ.

definition: Encryption that uses the same secret key to lock and unlock data.
exampleSentence: AES is the most common example of symmetric encryption in daily use.

definition: Encryption that uses a public key to lock and a private key to unlock data.
exampleSentence: Asymmetric encryption lets strangers send you secrets without sharing a password first.

definition: A value that proves who created data and that it has not been changed.
exampleSentence: The update is protected by a digital signature that the installer checks before running.

definition: Readable data that has not been encrypted.
exampleSentence: Never store passwords as plaintext in a database or in a log file.

definition: Data that has been encrypted and looks like random characters.
exampleSentence: Without the key, the ciphertext is just meaningless random-looking text.

definition: The secret half of a key pair that must never be shared.
exampleSentence: If someone steals your private key, they can pretend to be you.

definition: The shareable half of a key pair used to encrypt data or check signatures.
exampleSentence: You can publish your public key on your website without any risk.

definition: A matching public key and private key used together in asymmetric encryption.
exampleSentence: The server generated a new key pair when the certificate was renewed.

definition: A method for two parties to agree on a secret key over an insecure channel.
exampleSentence: The key exchange happens in the first milliseconds of every secure connection.

definition: The size of a key in bits, which affects how hard it is to break.
exampleSentence: A longer key length makes brute force attacks much more expensive.

definition: Regularly replacing encryption keys with new ones to limit the damage of a leak.
exampleSentence: Automatic key rotation replaces our encryption keys every ninety days.

definition: Creating, storing, using and retiring encryption keys safely.
exampleSentence: Strong encryption is useless without careful key management.

definition: Random data added to a password before hashing so equal passwords look different.
exampleSentence: A unique salt makes pre-built attack tables useless for stolen passwords.

definition: A secret value added to passwords before hashing and stored outside the database.
exampleSentence: The pepper is kept in a separate vault, not next to the hashed passwords.

definition: A precomputed table of hashes used to quickly reverse simple passwords.
exampleSentence: A rainbow table can crack unsalted passwords in just a few seconds.

definition: A situation where two different inputs produce the same hash value.
exampleSentence: Researchers found a hash collision, so the old algorithm is no longer trusted.

definition: A small value calculated from data to detect errors or changes.
exampleSentence: Verify the checksum of the download before you install the program.

definition: The fixed-size output created by a hash function from a message.
exampleSentence: The message digest is signed instead of the whole large document.

definition: A code that uses a secret key and a hash to check message authenticity.
exampleSentence: The API checks the HMAC to confirm that the request really came from our partner.

definition: A fast and widely used symmetric encryption algorithm.
exampleSentence: The laptop disk is protected with AES using a 256-bit key.

definition: A popular asymmetric algorithm used for encryption and digital signatures.
exampleSentence: The old system still signs its tokens with a short RSA key.

definition: A modern kind of asymmetric cryptography that offers strong security with short keys.
exampleSentence: Mobile devices prefer ECC because it needs less power and smaller keys.

definition: A method for two parties to create a shared secret over a public channel.
exampleSentence: The Diffie-Hellman exchange lets two strangers agree on a secret key in public.

definition: A cipher that encrypts data in fixed-size blocks.
exampleSentence: AES is a block cipher that works on sixteen bytes at a time.

definition: A cipher that encrypts data one bit or byte at a time.
exampleSentence: A stream cipher is a good choice for encrypting live video calls.

definition: A random starting value that makes each encryption of the same data different.
exampleSentence: Reusing an initialization vector can leak patterns in the encrypted data.

definition: A number used only once to prevent replay and reuse in cryptographic protocols.
exampleSentence: Each request includes a unique nonce so that old messages cannot be replayed.

definition: A measure of randomness, important for creating strong keys and passwords.
exampleSentence: A new virtual machine may have low entropy right after it starts.

definition: A tool that produces unpredictable numbers needed for keys and tokens.
exampleSentence: A weak random number generator made the session tokens easy to guess.

definition: The study of breaking or weakening encryption systems.
exampleSentence: Cryptanalysis of the old algorithm revealed several serious weaknesses.

definition: A calculation that is easy to perform but practically impossible to reverse.
exampleSentence: Hashing is a one-way function, so you cannot recover a password from it.

definition: Making code or data hard to read, which is not the same as real encryption.
exampleSentence: Obfuscation slows reverse engineers down, but it does not replace real security.

definition: Hiding secret data inside ordinary files such as images or audio.
exampleSentence: With steganography, the attacker hid a message in the pixels of a photo.

definition: Encryption where only the sender and receiver can read the message.
exampleSentence: With end-to-end encryption, even the service provider cannot read your chats.

definition: Encrypting stored data on disks, databases and backups.
exampleSentence: Encryption at rest protects the database files if somebody steals the drive.

definition: Encrypting data while it moves across a network.
exampleSentence: Encryption in transit stops people on the same network from reading your traffic.

definition: Hiding real values, like card numbers, by replacing them with fake characters.
exampleSentence: Data masking shows only the last four digits of the card on the screen.

definition: An algorithm used to encrypt and decrypt information.
exampleSentence: Each cipher is designed so that attackers cannot break it with today's computers.

definition: A mathematical method used for encryption, hashing or signing.
exampleSentence: Only an approved cryptographic algorithm may be used in our products.
